svg.desc: Step-specific guided recreation. Not a genuine screenshot or live result.
svg.text: INSTRUCTIONAL MOCKUP — NOT A LIVE CAPTURE OR RESULT
Get the expired-certificate fixture helper
Your Windows 10 host · Windows PowerShell
Windows PowerShell — Windows host
COMMAND / FILE CONTENT TO ENTER — PRESERVE CASE
Invoke-WebRequest -Uri https://cloudseam.tech/tls-lab/make-expired-fixture.sh -OutFile
"$env:USERPROFILE\Documents\SONIC-TLS\make-expired-fixture.sh"
Get-FileHash -Algorithm SHA256 "$env:USERPROFILE\Documents\SONIC-TLS\make-expired-fixture.sh"
# Expected SHA256: EFA17EA1A43F1C869379CB44109D00D22DC98EDF019837CBE09CA798DFB66EF6
notepad "$env:USERPROFILE\Documents\SONIC-TLS\make-expired-fixture.sh"
scp "$env:USERPROFILE\Documents\SONIC-TLS\make-expired-fixture.sh" learner@10.90.0.20:~/make-
expired-fixture.sh
EXPECTED RESULT / SIMULATED CLUE — CHECK YOUR OWN MACHINE
The downloaded script hash matches the published value, and its reviewed copy is on TLS-CA01.
FOLLOW THE NUMBERED INSTRUCTIONS IN THE LESSON
1. In normal Windows PowerShell, download the course helper into your existing SONIC-TLS folder.
2. Compare its complete SHA256 hash with the value shown below. Then open it in Notepad and read it: it
creates a deliberately expired public certificate using your existing practice intermediate.
3. Only after reviewing it, copy the script to the CA with SCP. It is not a genuine DoD tool.
No real private key, real certificate result, production access or DoD endorsement is shown.
